answer: When k identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol aggregates their evidence and applies penalties proportional to k², so coordination raises the loss faster than the swarm grows. Each identity’s bonded escrow is slashable, while asymmetric capital depreciation makes recovery costly. A sybil operator therefore risks an exponential multiplier in total capital loss upon detection: the gale of correlated faults can sweep through an ocean of accounts along one evidentiary thread.
